chapter: Los Angeles in 1935: school, jam sessions and the hobo trip west
title: Leaving Tulsa high school after a football injury and finishing in Los Angeles
summary: He quit school after a hospital stay, hoboed to Los Angeles, and graduated easily at Jefferson High.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I think you were telling me that you went to high school where?

I went to elementary school, Booker T. Washington in Tulsa, junior high school in Tulsa, up to my graduation, two months before graduation, well, I'll say this again for clarity. I went to elementary school in Tulsa, Booker T. Washington, Carver Junior High, and then Booker T. Washington High School, and I quit school because I had been in the hospital due to a football accident, and the doctors advised me that -- told me at that time that whenever you've got a knot
on your head, it doesn't go away, it goes to the weakest part of your body.

Well, me being the smallest man on the team, one of those big 200-pounders stepped on my instep and a knot swell up on it, and it went to my appendix. So I went to the hospital. No visitors, from any of who I thought were my friends. No one come to see me but my mother and my grandmother, they would alternate.

So when I went back to school, I had to make up some subjects. Grammar, math, so while I was in summer school I took up some extra subjects and passed my own class, when the regular season started. Boy, when I got out of the hospital, the teacher would say, "Oh, it's so good to see you back." I say, "Yeah, you jive --." And the rest of the kids, "Hey, hey, hey." I say, "Yeah, un-huh." I looked at all of them out of the corners of my eyes, you know, because I was a participant in all of the artistic things like acting, and literature, you know, we'd do skits on "Macbeth" in literature class. And we had a thing called "Popular Airs," everybody would sing a popular song of that year, and we'd have harmonica bands and had a quartet that aped the Mills Brothers, you know. I thought we was doing something, you know. I come back from the hospital and everybody cold-shouldered me, you know?
So I was in a hurry to get away from there, so I quit two months before graduation, I was -- had my cap and gown
measured, my class ring and pin picked up, and hoboed out here and I could have started to school immediately and graduated mid-term, but they wouldn't give me a diploma.

Well, because I hadn't spent enough time in the school, six months, you know. So they sent to Oklahoma to get my credentials. Well, now, Art in Oklahoma was a half unit. Out here it was a full unit. And they only required something like 27 units to graduate from high school. (laughs) And I had 40-something. So I didn't have to do anything but go to my home room class in the morning, and check out in the afternoon, and I'd stay up all night, listening to musicians, and go to school, check in, go home and go to sleep and come back and check out, and I'm gone again.
